title: Bram and the Verdict
premise: Cyrus Winterbourne, the cathedral's aging archivist, discovers that the diary of Verity Ashcombe—who vanished eleven years ago and was declared dead—contains entries written after her disappearance, in handwriting that matches his own late wife's. As he investigates, he learns the crypt's lock was changed the night she vanished and that the town's most respected family, the Hallowells, paid for the cathedral's restoration with money meant for Verity. The diary leads him to conclude that Verity faked her death to escape Edmund Hallowell, who had killed before, but that she returned secretly each year on the anniversary—and this year, someone is waiting to finish what was started. At the anniversary dinner, Cyrus exposes Edmund using the diary's final entry as a trap; Verity emerges from hiding to testify, Edmund is arrested, and Cyrus chooses truth over the loyalty that kept the town silent, donating the Hallowell inheritance to fund a memorial in the crypt.
about_author: Quentin Sandoval is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of births, deaths, and quiet scandals in English cathedral archives. That experience left an enduring fascination with the secrets towns agree not to see.

chapters.title: The Lock That Changed
chapters.summary: Cyrus Winterbourne's POV. While cataloguing donations for the anniversary dinner, Cyrus finds Verity Ashcombe's diary in a bequest box—its entries continuing three years past her disappearance. He notices the crypt lock was replaced the night she vanished, a detail the police never pursued. The emotional beat is quiet dread: a man who has solved three 'accidents' recognizes the shape of a fourth that everyone chose to bury.

chapters.title: What the Hallowells Paid For
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, intercut with diary excerpts from Verity. Following the paper trail, Cyrus discovers the cathedral's lavish restoration was funded by misappropriated Ashcombe money, brokered by Edmund Hallowell—the same man who signed her death certificate. The diary reveals Verity feared him long before she disappeared. The beat is rising anger: charity built on theft, respectability built on silence.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Trap
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Realizing Verity has returned secretly every year on the anniversary—and that this year's dinner falls on it—Cyrus plants the diary's final entry where only her watcher will find it, then attends the dinner as bait. Edmund realizes Cyrus knows and corners him in the crypt. The climax: Cyrus confronts Edmund with eleven years of evidence as footsteps descend the stairs—Verity, alive, having come for the trap.

chapters.title: A Glass Raised to Truth
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, closing with Verity's testimony. Edmund is arrested; the town reels as its benefactor's crimes surface. Cyrus refuses the Hallowell inheritance offered to buy his silence, directing it instead to a memorial in the crypt bearing Verity's name among the living. The resolution's beat is costly peace: loyalty to people must yield to loyalty to truth, and survival finally means being seen.
